title: Optimize auto-tuner: incident follow-up and safe-apply playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: On 2026-02-27 an automated recommendation from the Optimize auto-tuner was applied to production without sufficient canary gating. The change combined an aggressive batching profile and a shortened KV cache TTL which, for a subset of production traffic shapes, produced increased tail latency and a transient token cost spike. This ticket documents the postmortem, immediate mitigations taken, and the new safe-apply playbook for future auto-tuner recommendations.
postmortem_findings: Auto-tuner generated a compound config: batch_size_bias + kv_cache_ttl reduction. Individually acceptable in simulations, but combination caused request coalescing patterns to change.
Safe-apply pipeline used a 'fast-path' global switch that rolled the config to all clusters due to a race between orchestrator and config-store write confirmation.
Canary stage existed but was mis-configured: threshold window was too short (30s) and the health checks ignored token-cost deltas, so regressions during slower-moving tail events weren’t caught.
Monitoring had no immediate automated rollback trigger for latency regressions where CPU/GPU utilization remained nominal—only errors and pod restarts triggered rollbacks.
Lack of a predictive cost delta estimate on the apply UI caused SRE to underestimate short-term burst costs for high-concurrency tenants.
Runbooks for Optimize autoscaling and cache TTL tuning were fragmented across Confluence pages, leading to delayed coordinated response between SRE and the Optimize team.
actions_taken: 2026-02-27 14:12 UTC: Manually rolled back the auto-config to previous stable values using emergency revert endpoint (rollback-id: rb-20260227-01).
2026-02-27 14:25 UTC: Throttled auto-tuner to review queue; disabled automatic apply for all Optimize recommendations until safe-apply fixes deployed.
2026-02-27 15:00 UTC: Opened incident channel #incident-optimize-autotune. Notified top-10 affected customers and customer success.
2026-02-28: Deployed patch to orchestrator to add write-confirmation handshake preventing concurrent global rollouts (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7264).
2026-03-03: Added a short-term monitoring rule to create alerts on per-tenant token-cost deltas > 40% within 10 minutes (Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/optimize/autotune-costs).
mitigations_and_playbook: Pre-apply simulation: run multi-tenant traffic replay against candidate config for 72 hours across representative workloads (batching + cache interactions).
Canary policy: default to 1% traffic for 30 minutes, then 5% for 2 hours, then 25% for 6 hours with explicit confirm step before global rollout.
Automated regression checks: block rollout if p99 latency increases > 10% or token cost per 1k requests increases > 25% in any canary window.
Safe-apply orchestration: require two-phase commit with config-store confirmation and per-region apply sequencing to avoid global race conditions.
Auto-rollback: implement a circuit-breaker to revert candidate configs automatically when regression triggers fire; notify SRE and authoring engineer.
UI changes: surface predicted cost delta and estimated tail-latency risk on every auto-tune recommendation (UI mock: https://figma.com/file/optimize-autotune-mock).

Runbook steps (short): 1) Pause auto-tuner, 2) Assess affected tenants, 3) Rollback if still present, 4) Create canary config and run replay, 5) Re-enable auto-applies only after successful 72h replay and manual sign-off.
next_steps: ENG-4830: Implement two-phase commit for config applies (owner: Diego Ramos; estimate: 3).
ENG-4831: Add predictive cost estimator to Optimize UI and recommendation APIs (owner: Aisha Patel; estimate: 5).
Add full traffic replay harness to CI that runs combos of batching+cache configs against recorded sessions (owner: SRE; target milestone: 2026-04-01).
Consolidate runbooks into a single Optimize Incident playbook with clear roles: SRE lead, Optimize author, PM communications owner (doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPT/Autotune+Playbook).
Schedule a cross-team blameless review on 2026-03-15 to validate the playbook and sign off on canary thresholds.
